tweets: Calling external contracts can transfer control before your function finishes, allowing another contract to execute first.
This creates a reentrancy attack where the malicious contract calls back into you before the original call completes.
Different invocations of your function may then interact in ways that were not intended by your logic.
To prevent this, perform all internal state changes before making any external calls.
This approach is known as the Checks-Effects-Interactions pattern.
Alternatively, you can use a reentrancy lock like OpenZeppelin's ReentrancyGuard to mitigate the risk.
